evidence_summary: OECD Health at a Glance 2025 supports the high-level health cost benchmark: US government/compulsory health spending is far above the OECD average, with the compulsory-scope caveat recorded in the source ledger.

Papanicolas, Woskie, and Jha support the source-packet hypothesis that US health cost pressure is substantially about prices and administrative costs rather than only utilization; the paper is literature evidence, not a current federal scoring model.
CBO long-term outlook supports the federal budget-pressure context for major health programs and Medicare; projections must be labeled as projections.
CMS Medicare Trustees 2026 supports Medicare part-financing and enrollment context, but does not by itself identify a provider-price savings estimate.
metric_candidates: government/compulsory health spending as percent of GDP versus OECD average, with scope caveat
provider/facility/procedure/drug price index versus benchmark after quality, access, and case-mix controls
administrative share or billing complexity indicator for affected programs
Medicare Part A/B/D expenditure or government-support per enrollee with source-year basis visible
outcome_floor_checks: Coverage, access, and health outcomes must be preserved or improved.
Program-specific quality and case-mix controls must be attached before comparing prices.
Medicare HI, Part B, and Part D financing streams must stay separate.
No estimate can reduce care volume or eligibility unless a reviewed source shows the outcome floor remains protected.
missing_before_estimate: CMS or HHS program-specific price/utilization extraction for selected services, drugs, or provider categories
chosen benchmark and case-mix adjustment method
reviewed quality, access, and outcome floor sources for the affected population
CBO, CMS, or other reviewed scoring method that converts the lever into a savings estimate without double counting
public_use_rule: Use as a source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: OECD Health at a Glance 2025 supports the high-level health cost benchmark that motivates administrative simplification work, with the government/compulsory scope caveat visible.

Papanicolas, Woskie, and Jha support the source-packet hypothesis that administrative costs are one of the major US health cost drivers; the paper is literature evidence, not a current administrative-savings score.
CBO long-term outlook supports the budget-pressure context for major health programs and Medicare, but does not by itself score billing simplification savings.

CMS Medicare Trustees 2026 supports Medicare financing and enrollment context for future per-enrollee administrative metrics, but does not isolate billing, prior authorization, or claims-processing savings.
metric_candidates: administrative cost or processing burden per covered person with program scope visible
claims-processing cycle time, denial/rework rate, and appeal volume with access floor
prior-authorization or billing-touch count per episode, claim, provider, or enrollee
Medicare Part A/B/D administrative metric candidates kept separate by financing and enrollment basis
outcome_floor_checks: Coverage access, payment accuracy, and beneficiary/provider service levels must remain preserved.
Simplification cannot remove payment-integrity controls without replacement evidence.
Beneficiaries must retain lawful notice, appeal, and due-process protections.
Provider administrative relief must not increase improper payments or delay eligible care.
missing_before_estimate: CMS or HHS program-specific administrative-cost extraction for selected programs or claims workflows
baseline volume for billing, authorization, denial, appeal, and rework steps
access, payment-accuracy, service-level, and due-process floor sources
reviewed scoring method that converts administrative simplification into net savings without double counting price or utilization reforms
public_use_rule: Use as a source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: CBO long-term outlook supports the debt, deficit, and net-interest trajectory that motivates a primary-balance work item; projections must remain labeled as projections.
OMB Historical Table 1.2 supports annual federal receipts, outlays, deficits, and GDP-share context for fiscal-balance framing.
OMB Historical Table 3.2 supports the FY2025 gross Treasury interest spend-category row, but does not by itself score future debt-service reduction.
Treasury Debt to the Penny supports debt-stock context after query-date locking; it is dynamic and must not be merged into annual projections without year-basis labels.
metric_candidates: primary deficit or surplus as percent of GDP under stated policy assumptions
debt held by the public as percent of GDP with projection label
net interest as percent of GDP and share of outlays
gross Treasury interest outlays kept visible as financing cost, not program benefit
outcome_floor_checks: Debt service must remain paid in full and on time.
Fiscal changes must preserve lawful commitments and explicit program outcome floors.
Primary-balance scenarios must not reclassify interest as a discretionary program cut.
Projection, fiscal-year, and daily debt-stock bases must remain labeled separately.
missing_before_estimate: chosen CBO, OMB, or Treasury scoring baseline and projection window
policy-specific revenue and spending assumptions
debt-stock path and interest-rate assumptions tied to the same scenario
reviewed rule for translating primary-balance changes into debt-service changes without double counting
public_use_rule: Use as a source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: CBO long-term outlook supports the projected net-interest pressure context and interest-rate sensitivity framing; projections must remain labeled.
Treasury Debt to the Penny supports current debt-stock context after query-date locking.
Treasury Average Interest Rates on Treasury Securities supports rate-context monitoring for marketable and non-marketable securities, but does not by itself estimate avoidable interest costs.
OMB Historical Table 3.2 supports the FY2025 gross Treasury interest outlay context and keeps interest visible as a financing cost.
metric_candidates: weighted average Treasury interest rate by security class with query date
debt-stock and debt-held-by-public level with daily source basis visible
net interest or gross Treasury interest as percent of GDP and share of outlays
scenario exposure to refinancing, rate, and maturity assumptions
outcome_floor_checks: Treasury market functioning and debt service reliability must remain preserved.
Maturity/rate-risk monitoring must not imply default, delayed payment, or unpaid debt service.
Dynamic Treasury query dates and annual OMB/CBO fiscal-year bases must stay separate.
Any debt-management scenario must be sourced to reviewed Treasury/CBO analysis before public use.
missing_before_estimate: query-locked Treasury debt-stock and average-rate extracts
maturity distribution or refinancing exposure source suitable for the scenario
reviewed CBO or Treasury interest-rate assumptions for the same horizon
scoring method that converts maturity/rate exposure into risk context without claiming savings
public_use_rule: Use as a source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: GAO Weapon Systems Annual Assessment 2025 supports acquisition-program risk and leading-practices context for procurement-control work; it does not by itself score savings.
CBO 2025 FYDP long-term implications supports planned defense-cost trajectory and projection context; projections must remain labeled.
OMB Historical Table 6.1 supports national-defense outlays as percent of GDP on the OMB budget-function basis, not NATO/SIPRI basis.
NATO defense expenditure data supports international defense-burden context, with NATO-definition caveats.
metric_candidates: program cost growth and schedule variance against approved baseline
share of major programs meeting knowledge, design, and production leading-practice indicators
defense outlays as percent of GDP on OMB function-050 basis
FYDP projected cost path versus appropriated and executed spending
outcome_floor_checks: Readiness, strategy commitments, alliance obligations, and service-member commitments must remain preserved.
Savings cannot be booked from deferred capability without a reviewed strategy decision.
OMB, NATO, and CBO defense bases must stay labeled separately.
Program-specific estimates require acquisition baseline and readiness evidence.
missing_before_estimate: program-level acquisition baseline and current cost/schedule extract
readiness and strategy floor source for affected capabilities
reviewed scoring method that converts control improvements into net savings
role-reviewed wording before any waste, performance, or acquisition-failure public claim
public_use_rule: Use as a source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: DoD OIG FY2025 audit-results summary supports audit-control context, including material weaknesses and control issues, but does not by itself estimate savings.
GAO Weapon Systems Annual Assessment 2025 supports acquisition-control context that can be paired with audit-control closure work.
OMB Historical Table 6.1 supports national-defense scale and GDP-share context for prioritizing control work.
metric_candidates: open versus closed material weaknesses, significant deficiencies, and noncompliance instances
repeat audit finding count and corrective-action aging
asset accountability and financial-statement audit progress indicators
control-remediation milestones tied to readiness and mission execution floor
outcome_floor_checks: Controls must improve accountability without degrading lawful mission execution or readiness.
Audit-control closure must not be described as direct savings until a reviewed estimate exists.
Material weaknesses are control findings, not automatically fraud, waste, or abuse findings.
Corrective-action status must be source-backed before public progress claims.
missing_before_estimate: detailed audit finding/control inventory with corrective-action status
repeat-finding and closure-date extraction
mission/readiness floor evidence for affected control areas
reviewed scoring method before treating control closure as savings
public_use_rule: Use as a source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: GAO High-Risk Series 2025 supports the disaster-assistance pressure surface: federal disaster assistance was added as a new high-risk area because disasters are becoming costlier and more frequent and federal relief needs to be delivered efficiently and effectively.
FEMA BRIC supports pre-disaster hazard-mitigation program context, but does not by itself prove a project-level avoided-loss estimate.

OpenFEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance Projects supports query-locked project-level mitigation records, including project amount, federal share, benefit-cost ratio, status, program area, and geography fields.

OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries supports event-level declaration context beginning in 1953 and can anchor disaster frequency, geography, declaration type, and authorized recovery-program fields.
OMB Historical Table 3.2 supports the FY2025 disaster relief and insurance outlay subfunction, but one fiscal year is lumpy and must not be used alone as a waste finding.
metric_candidates: mitigation project cost versus source-backed expected avoided loss or exposure reduction
event frequency and geographic recurrence using FEMA disaster declarations
federal relief outlays by disaster, account, program, and fiscal year with event linkage
resilience indicators tied to the same hazard, geography, and beneficiary floor
outcome_floor_checks: Emergency response, recovery capacity, and lawful aid commitments must remain preserved.
Mitigation work cannot delay or narrow lawful emergency response.
Avoided-loss claims require project-level benefit-cost or reviewed scoring evidence.
Equity, access, and local-capacity effects must be checked before shifting costs to state, local, tribal, territorial, or household actors.
missing_before_estimate: benefit-cost method details behind query-locked FEMA mitigation project records
project-level benefit-cost or avoided-loss method tied to the same hazard and geography
event-to-account bridge from declaration records to federal outlays
reviewed emergency-response and lawful-aid floor sources for affected communities
public_use_rule: Use as a disaster-mitigation source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: OMB Historical Table 3.2 supports the annual disaster relief and insurance subfunction, but does not identify which costs are recurring exposure versus one-time emergency response.
Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement supports current-period receipt and outlay context after query-date and period locking; it is not a substitute for the OMB annual spine.
USAspending supports program, account, and award exploration after query parameters are recorded, but dynamic search results must not be cited without a locked extract.
OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries supplies event identifiers, declaration types, dates, programs, and geography that can be used to tag disaster outlays over time.
GAO High-Risk Series 2025 supports the need to improve federal disaster-assistance delivery and data sharing, including fragmentation across federal entities.
metric_candidates: share of disaster outlays tagged by event, account, agency, program, and supplemental appropriation
recurring-exposure versus one-time emergency-response classification with source-backed rule
lag from declaration, obligation, and award to outlay by program and fiscal year
unlinked or unclassified disaster spending share after query-locked extracts
outcome_floor_checks: Transparency work must not delay emergency response or lawful recovery aid.
Recurring-exposure labels must not deny legitimate one-time relief or survivor assistance.
OMB annual, Treasury monthly, USAspending dynamic, and FEMA event-record bases must remain labeled separately.
Any public claim about poor tracking or waste requires reviewed finding language, not just unlinked records.
missing_before_estimate: query-locked Treasury, USAspending, and FEMA extracts with periods and parameters recorded
event-to-account and supplemental-to-base budget crosswalk
definition of recurring exposure versus one-time emergency response reviewed against agency sources
reviewed scoring method before treating better tracking as savings
public_use_rule: Use as a supplemental-tracking source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, fraud, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: OMB PaymentAccuracy.gov supports program-level improper-payment rates, dollar estimates, reduction targets, and corrective-action context where agencies report under payment-integrity law.

GAO improper-payment reporting supports the government-wide improper-payment pressure surface, including FY2024 reporting of $161.5B and cumulative estimates of about $2.8T since FY2003; these are estimates and include overpayments, underpayments, and unknown-payment status depending on program methodology.
Treasury Do Not Pay supports pre-payment and post-payment matching context for identifying potential improper payments, but match results must be reviewed before any program-specific finding.
OMB Historical Table 8.5 supports mandatory-program outlay scale for affected benefit programs, but eligibility, access, and beneficiary claims must come from program sources.
metric_candidates: program improper-payment rate, amount, root cause, and reduction target from PaymentAccuracy.gov
overpayment, underpayment, unknown-payment, and eligibility-error categories kept separate
pre-payment match, stop, recovery, false-positive, and appeal/reversal rates
benefit access, denial, timeliness, and due-process indicators after control changes
outcome_floor_checks: Controls must not create unlawful denial, access barriers, or benefit delays for eligible people.
Improper-payment estimates are not automatically fraud, waste, abuse, or collectible savings.
Pre-payment matches require review, privacy, accuracy, and appeal safeguards before public claims.
Program-specific methodology and confidence limits must be visible before comparing rates or dollars.
missing_before_estimate: query-locked PaymentAccuracy.gov program extracts with fiscal year and methodology notes
program-specific root-cause and corrective-action records
access, denial, appeal, reversal, and timeliness floor evidence for affected beneficiaries
reviewed scoring method that converts control changes into net savings without double counting or shifting lawful benefits
public_use_rule: Use as a payment-integrity source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of fraud, waste, abuse, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.

evidence_summary: SSA performance reporting supports claims-processing and service-level context, including retirement, survivors, disability, phone, and field-office service indicators where reported.
SSA open-data disability processing time supports monthly average processing-time tracking for combined Title II disability and Title XVI blind/disabled claims, excluding technical denials.
VA detailed claims data supports veterans-claims inventory, backlog, accuracy, and timeliness context for a benefits-processing floor.
GAO improper-payment reporting supports the link between payment integrity and administrative processes, but does not by itself score claims-timeliness savings.
metric_candidates: average processing time and backlog volume by program, claim type, and period
accuracy, denial, appeal, reversal, and rework indicators paired with processing-time metrics
staffing, automation, manual-touch, and administrative-cost indicators where agency sources expose them
service-access floor metrics such as lawful notice, due process, call/field-office access, and beneficiary burden
outcome_floor_checks: Timely access, lawful notice, and due-process protections must remain preserved for eligible people.
Faster processing cannot be booked as savings if accuracy, appeal rights, or eligible access degrade.
SSA, VA, and other agency timeliness bases must stay separate by program, claim type, and period.
Public claims about backlogs, poor service, or waste require source-specific reviewed wording.
missing_before_estimate: query-locked SSA and VA processing-time and backlog extracts
administrative cost and staffing/process records tied to the same claims workflows
accuracy, appeal, reversal, and beneficiary-access floor evidence
reviewed scoring method that converts process improvement into net savings or service gains without denying lawful benefits
public_use_rule: Use as a claims-timeliness source packet only; not a savings estimate and not a finding of waste, poor performance, or legal dedication of income-tax dollars.
